high.title: Vietnamese Stock Market Receives New Support Signal — What Do Experts Say?
high.summary: Mr. Nguyen The Minh, Head of Retail Client Analysis at An Binh Securities (ABS), notes that the VN-Index remains in an uptrend, though its relative strength has eased — declining from 87 to 83 points — meaning Vietnam has slipped out of the global top-10 strongest markets. Critically, the index holding above the 80-point threshold suggests the broader uptrend remains intact. A sharp decline in the US VIX index signals improving global risk sentiment, creating a more favorable environment for risk assets including Vietnamese equities. Of particular significance for capital flow watchers: while global equity funds saw net outflows of ~$14 billion last week (driven primarily by US profit-taking after a strong rally), capital continues to flow into non-US markets — especially Asian emerging markets. This is a meaningful tailwind for the VN-Index and VND-denominated assets. Fund managers should monitor whether this EM Asia rotation translates into sustained foreign buying on the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (HOSE), which would support both equity valuations and VND demand.

high.title: Over 12 Billion Bank Shares Set to Hit the Market: Techcombank and VPBank Lead the Way
high.summary: Vietnam's banking sector is entering a historic capital expansion cycle in 2026, with more than 12 billion new bank shares expected to be issued — the largest issuance volume in the sector's history. Techcombank leads with a planned 60% stock dividend (approximately 4.25 billion new shares), which would lift its charter capital above VND 113,000 billion. VPBank follows with a 26.04% equity-sourced share issuance, targeting a capital raise from ~VND 79,340 billion to ~VND 100,000 billion. For bond and equity investors, this wave of capital raising is highly relevant: increased bank capital buffers may reduce credit risk premiums on bank-issued bonds; however, significant share dilution could weigh on near-term equity valuations. The supply overhang of 12+ billion new shares is a key technical headwind for the banking sub-index on HOSE. Investors should track regulatory approval timelines and monitor whether institutional demand is sufficient to absorb this supply without pressuring prices.

high.title: Deposit Rates Heat Up: Is the Race to Attract Capital a Cause for Concern?
high.summary:
A notable tightening in Vietnam's deposit funding market is underway, with several smaller banks quietly raising deposit rates beyond official posted schedules through preferential programs and off-schedule agreements. Survey data shows certain banks offering rates as high as **9.0%/year for 6-month tenors** and **9.2–9.3%/year for 12-month tenors**. Among publicly advertised promotions for July, SeABank is offering up to **8.55%/year** and digital bank Cake by VPBank up to **8.9%/year**.

The pressure extends into the bond market: in late June, several banks issued bonds at multi-year high coupon rates. Notably, **Vietbank offered 9.7%/year** on two tranches totalling VND 1,500 billion, while **Bao Viet Bank successfully placed VND 2,000 billion at 9.6%/year**.

high.title: Rising Deposit Rates: How Much Have Households and Businesses Deposited into the Banking System?
high.summary:
As of June 26, 2026, deposit mobilization across Vietnamese credit institutions grew 5.02% YTD — below last year's comparable pace of 6.11%. Credit growth also moderated to 7.41%, versus 8.3% a year prior. Despite the slowdown in growth rates, the absolute inflow is substantial: an estimated VND 830 trillion (~USD 32–33bn) in new deposits was added in H1 2026, bringing total system deposits past VND 16.5 quadrillion. The catalyst is a sharp rise in deposit rates: publicly advertised 12-month rates now sit at 7.0–7.5% p.a., but numerous banks are quietly offering 8.5–9.0% p.a. for 6–12 month tenors, particularly targeting new or VIP clients. **Key implications:** The divergence between headline and effective deposit rates signals intense competition for liquidity and potential margin pressure on banks. Rising deposit rates structurally push up lending costs, complicating SBV's efforts to keep credit affordable. For bond traders, elevated deposit rates competing with government bond yields is a key dynamic to monitor — any re-rating of risk-free yields would impact VGB pricing directly. Watch whether SBV responds with open market operations to ease liquidity tightness.

---

high.title: Bank Deposit Interest Rates on July 6 at Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank, MB, Sacombank, HDBank...
high.summary: A survey of online deposit rates as of July 6 shows Vietnamese banks maintaining the interest rate framework established in late June, with no material changes signaling a shift in monetary policy direction. ACB leads the market at 7.3%/year for 12-month deposits, followed by Saigonbank at 7.2%/year for the same tenor. Six banks are now offering rates at or above 7.0%/year for 12-month deposits (MBV, VCBNeo, PGBank, VIB, ACB, Saigonbank), while the Big 4 state-owned banks (Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank) maintain structurally lower rates.

medium.title: Securities Stocks Break Out Across the Board — Experts Weigh In on Whether VN-Index Is Entering a New Uptrend
medium.summary: Securities-sector stocks staged a notable recovery in the last session of the prior week, sparking market debate about whether the VN-Index is on the cusp of a new bullish leg. Bui Van Huy, Deputy Director at FIDT, urges caution, noting that brokerage stocks typically lead in genuine bull cycles — acting as early signals of improving liquidity conditions and risk appetite — but a one- to two-session bounce following a sharp drawdown does not confirm a trend reversal. He highlights that many securities names fell 20–40% from their peaks during the recent correction, making the current move more consistent with a technical rebound than a structural re-rating. For equity investors, the key watch points are sustained daily trading volume, broader market breadth beyond the securities sub-sector, and whether institutional flows return with conviction. The article is relevant as securities-sector performance is a leading indicator for VN-Index momentum and overall market risk sentiment.

medium.title: Equities, Gold, or Real Estate: How Should Portfolios Be Allocated in H2 2026?
medium.summary: FIDT's Deputy Director Bui Van Huy outlines his strategic asset allocation framework for H2 2026, centered on Vietnam's ambitious ~12% GDP growth target for the second half of the year. He argues that both public-sector fiscal stimulus and private-sector mobilization toward this growth objective create selective investment opportunities, but cautions against aggressive re-risking based purely on near-term earnings season optimism. His recommended approach is phased deployment of capital, maintaining a liquidity reserve while identifying long-horizon positions. Sector preferences include banking, retail, and leading conglomerates pivoting from pure real estate toward broader asset ownership platforms. For international fund managers, the banking sector callout is directly relevant — sustained credit growth to support a 12% GDP target implies upward pressure on lending volumes, potential NIM dynamics, and sensitivity to any SBV policy rate adjustments in H2.

medium.title: The AI Frenzy Inflates Global Stock Market Capitalization — Where Does Vietnam Stand?
medium.summary: Global equity market capitalization surged meaningfully in H1 2026, driven predominantly by the AI investment wave and associated semiconductor supply chain boom — despite ongoing geopolitical uncertainty, trade tensions, and a less accommodative Fed rate path. S&P Global Market Intelligence data show multi-trillion-dollar market cap gains in the US, South Korea, Taiwan, Japan, and select European markets. Vietnam's equity market posted positive but modest gains in H1, led by a handful of large-cap stocks, though the market's overall scale remains limited relative to regional peers. For VN-Index investors, this global context matters: if risk appetite globally continues to be supported by the AI theme and capital flows into emerging market equities resume, Vietnam could benefit from incremental foreign portfolio inflows — a key FX and equity market catalyst to monitor in H2 2026.

medium.title: World Gold Council Assesses Gold Unlikely to Fall Sharply — What Is the Highest Price Scenario?
medium.summary:
Gold had a dramatic start to 2026, spiking to record highs above $5,500/oz in January before retreating below $4,000/oz by end of June — still among the best-performing assets year-to-date despite a ~7% drawdown. The World Gold Council (WGC) highlights growing sensitivity to geopolitical risks and a rising influence of Asian markets in gold price discovery. For Vietnam, gold price dynamics are directly relevant to domestic monetary conditions: elevated domestic gold prices historically drive VND demand for gold imports, pressure the trade balance, and complicate SBV's FX management. The WGC's view that gold is unlikely to see a deep decline suggests continued upward pressure on Vietnam's domestic gold market, which warrants monitoring for potential SBV intervention or policy responses.

medium.title: Bank Deposit Rates as of July 5 at Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank, MB, Sacombank, HDBank...
medium.summary:
As of July 5, official posted deposit rate schedules at most banks showed little change from end-June levels, with state-owned banks (Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank) holding rates steady. Among private banks, **ACB leads the market at 7.3%/year for 12-month deposits**, followed by Saigonbank at 7.2%/year. Only six banks currently post rates at or above 7.0%/year for 12-month tenors, including MBV, PGBank, VCBNeo, and VIB. This snapshot suggests that while off-schedule and negotiated rates are rising sharply (as reported in Article 2), official listed rates remain relatively anchored — a divergence that may reflect competitive pressure building beneath the surface. For fund managers, this gap between listed and effective rates is a key indicator to watch for signs of broader rate repricing.

---

medium.title: MASVN Expert: VN-Index in Accumulation Phase, Two Key Sectors Expected to Attract Capital Flows
medium.summary: Mirae Asset Securities Vietnam (MASVN) analyst Tran Quoc Toan characterizes the VN-Index's H2 2026 trajectory as "accumulative upward" — anticipating intermittent volatility rather than a sharp rally, but with a structurally bullish long-term bias. The key supports cited include: recovery of core corporate earnings, deeper credit growth transmission into the economy in H2, banking sector liquidity support measures, and continued FDI inflows and public investment disbursement. Importantly, the analyst flags that moderating interest rates would provide meaningful additional upside for equities. The key risk highlighted is persistent net foreign selling, which remains a significant overhang for the market. For fund managers, this outlook reinforces a cautiously constructive stance on Vietnamese equities, while the foreign outflow risk warrants close monitoring of capital flow data and VND stability.

medium.title: From July 1st, Banks Must Report Account Balances and Abnormal Transactions to Tax Authorities
medium.summary: Under Decree 252, effective July 1, 2026, all Vietnamese credit institutions, foreign bank branches, and payment service providers are now legally required to share taxpayer account information — including account balances, transaction volumes, values, and cross-border transfer details — with tax authorities on a monthly basis (by the 10th of the following month). This represents a significant tightening of financial transparency and tax compliance infrastructure in Vietnam. For capital flow monitoring purposes, mandatory reporting of cross-border transaction details may affect the structuring of inbound FDI, remittance flows, and potentially foreign portfolio investment. While primarily a tax enforcement measure, it adds a layer of regulatory scrutiny over banking transactions that international fund managers should factor into their operational and compliance frameworks.

medium.title: Gold Ring and Gold Bar Prices – Afternoon of July 6th
medium.summary: Domestic gold prices on July 6 remained broadly stable: SJC gold bars were quoted at VND 148.0–151.0 million/tael across major retailers (SJC, DOJI, PNJ, Bao Tin Manh Hai), while 24K gold rings were priced at VND 147.9–150.9 million/tael. International spot gold was trading at approximately USD 4,174/oz with limited movement. HSBC's view cited in the article notes that while a strong USD and elevated US Treasury yields cap gold's upside, central bank purchasing and portfolio diversification demand remain supportive. Gold price dynamics in Vietnam are a secondary but relevant FX indicator — persistent domestic gold premiums can signal VND depreciation pressure and informal demand for hard assets, so traders should monitor any widening of the spread between domestic and international gold prices.

medium.title: Fastest-Growing Banks by Capital Over the Past 10 Years: One Bank Grew Nearly 10x, Vietcombank Takes the Lead
medium.summary:
Total charter capital across 27 Vietnamese commercial banks surged more than 3.5x over the decade 2015–2025, rising from VND 260,600 billion to nearly VND 922,000 billion — an increase of over VND 661,000 billion. Capital growth has been driven by stock dividends, private placements, rights issues, and ESOP schemes, reflecting the sector's push to meet Basel capital adequacy standards, expand credit capacity, and fund digital transformation. VPBank leads among private banks in percentage growth, while Vietcombank now holds the top position in absolute charter capital terms. The capital build-up is broadly positive for banking sector stability and systemic resilience, reducing tail risk for VND and government bond markets. For equity investors, continued capital expansion may signal further share issuances, which could weigh on book value per share but enhances longer-term lending headroom and ROE potential.
